_comment: Model roster and context arms. Roster rule: models released within roughly the last two months at freeze time - a benchmark of current tooling should run current models. Tier names are how charts group models; exact model ids are pinned at freeze time. Meta models route through OpenRouter (no native Meta provider in leviath yet). The mockx entry exists only for offline smoke runs against the deterministic script provider.
_released: Release dates are the date the model became generally available on its API; for the GPT-5.6 family that is the 2026-07-09 general launch, not the 2026-06-26 limited-preview announcement. run_quality.py records each model's age at round start in round.json.

Kimi K3.override_reason: pin for reproducibility: since leviath 0.3.3 (#360) the runtime primes windows from OpenRouter /models at daemon start, but that lookup is live state, can time out (10s), and often omits max_output_tokens - a frozen round pins both instead of measuring whatever the API served that day

Muse Spark 1.2.override_reason: pin for reproducibility: since leviath 0.3.3 (#360) the runtime primes windows from OpenRouter /models at daemon start, but that lookup is live state, can time out (10s), and often omits max_output_tokens - a frozen round pins both instead of measuring whatever the API served that day

Grok 4.6.override_reason: pin for reproducibility: OpenRouter reports a 500k window and no max_completion_tokens for this model; the round pins both rather than measuring whatever the live lookup serves
Grok 4.6._note: cross-vendor critic for the CRS flagship: a genuinely different lab attacking the planner's plan. Verify with a capability cell before any counted round.

arms.name: flat-compacting
arms.note: strong flat baseline: the same single window, but it compacts on overflow (summarize-oldest) instead of evicting - what production harnesses actually do. Generated from the flat blueprint by make_flat.py; check_pairs.py asserts the overflow strategy is the only difference.

arms.name: structured-mix-adversarial-scoped
arms.note: Scoping and the plan critic together: the two changes have only ever been measured separately.

arms.name: structured-mix-flagship
arms.note: The composed configuration - scoped layout, adversarial plan review, cross-vendor stage assignment. Not an ablation arm: it moves several variables at once on purpose, and is read against the ablation arms, not instead of them.

arms.name: structured-mix-sonnet-loop
arms.note: flagship with the loop stage on the workhorse model.

arms.name: flat-pinned-hardened
arms.note: flat baseline + the wind-down and result-hygiene discipline production harnesses carry; the variance-decomposition arm for the collapse study

arms.name: flat-compacting-hardened
arms.note: the compacting baseline with the same hardening

_context_window: Context window in tokens, pinned per model and written into the runtime's config as a model_capabilities override. Region budgets are percentages of the window, so the window decides how big every region is. Since 0.3.3 (#360) the runtime primes OpenRouter windows from the provider at daemon start, so the override is no longer a bug workaround - it is a freeze: the round pins the window it measured under rather than inheriting whatever /models returned that day (the priming also frequently lacks max_output_tokens). Each value here was verified against the provider, and the resolved window is recorded in every round.
_arms: Mixed arms name a generated variant (blueprints/mixes.json): the same agent with one model named per stage. The grid crosses the model in the loop stages, which carry the token spend, with the model in the stages that decide and check, which are few calls over small contexts: econ = economy loops + workhorse thinking, frontier-brain = economy loops + frontier thinking, muse-sonnet / muse-opus = the same with the coding-oriented economy model, sonnet-opus = workhorse loops + frontier thinking.
_rate_limits: What each provider account is allowed to sustain, declared here and written into the runtime's config so the daemon paces itself instead of discovering the limit as rejected requests. These are deliberately conservative placeholders: replace each with the tier limits on the account actually being billed before a counted round, since a round that was throttled measures the throttling as much as the agent. The values are frozen with the round and recorded, because what a round promised to stay under is part of what it measured.
_probes: Context Retention Suite probe configuration, frozen with the round. Every replay probe - for every arm - is answered by the one reader_model, so the retention curve compares context states rather than the models that produced them; the reader is a third-vendor model no arm uses for its loop stages. The grader_model is a different vendor than the reader. Both are roster labels; ids and rates resolve through the same tables as the arms.
